From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2024-09-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Audit logging & compliance follow-up (ClearPath / Redwood)

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the call today — I appreciated the candid questions from you and Jason. Quick recap and a short list of follow-ups so your security/compliance team has what they need for the vendor intake: 

- SOC 2: you asked whether we have a current Type II and what the scope is. I attached a one-page SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) — that doc includes the report date and the control scope. Happy to arrange direct contact with our auditor if they need to verify anything.

- GDPR / HIPAA: you mentioned data residency and PHI handling. Redwood supports private deployments and region pinning; for hosted we can route processing to US or EU regions and we have an available BAA for customers processing PHI.

- Audit logging & exportability: per our conversation, the two primary things you wanted confirmed were (1) what admin/activity and API logs we capture and (2) how those logs can be exported in an auditable (and immutable) way. I attached a short matrix (audit-logs-capabilities-matrix.xlsx) that outlines available events, retention defaults, and export delivery options (S3/GCS/Azure).

Can you confirm the following on your side so we scope the technical deep dive:
1) Will your auditors require a SOC 2 Type II PDF or something beyond the standard report?
2) Desired retention window for exported logs (months/years)?
3) Do you need immutability (WORM / Object Lock) or chain-of-custody attestation for exports?

Next steps I propose: 1) I’ll loop in our security lead to answer any nitty-gritty export/immutability questions, 2) schedule a 45-min technical demo of our audit export workflow (S3 export + Object Lock options), and 3) we’ll start the vendor questionnaire (if you want us to) and return it within 48 hours.

If you can share the vendor questionnaire now I’ll start filling it out — otherwise we can cover the high level on the demo.

Best,

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Ben — thanks for the recap and the attachments. Quick answers from our side: 

- We do need the SOC 2 Type II PDF (full report) for our procurement record. Please advise whether the auditor is comfortable sharing the report under an NDA — procurement may request that.

- Retention: for our use case we typically request 2 years of admin/activity history available for export. For incident response we may ask for shorter live retention but ability to pull archives back to 2 years.

- Immutability: yes, we would prefer exports that can be placed under Object Lock or another WORM process — for eDiscovery and regulatory hold scenarios.

On exports: would your S3/GCS export include the full event payloads (not just metadata)? Our forensics team prefers full request/response context where available, or at least payload hashes and request_id correlation. Also curious about supported formats (JSONL, Parquet?) and whether exports can include a signed manifest (checksums + timestamp) to prove integrity.

Attaching our standard vendor questionnaire — if you can start filling Section 3 (Audit & Logging) that would be helpful: ClearPath-vendor-questionnaire.pdf

We’ll aim to be ready for a technical demo next week. I’ll check Jason’s availability and propose times.

Thanks,

Elena Martin

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed questions. I’ll cover the technical pieces you raised so procurement/security has concrete answers for the vendor intake form. I’ll keep this high-level and can expand on any item during the demo.

1) SOC 2 & sharing
- We completed a SOC 2 Type II with a scope that includes our hosted control plane and inference runtime (report date: 2024-06). We can share the full report under NDA; our auditor is contactable for verification.

2) HIPAA / BAA
- We offer a BAA for customers handling PHI. For hosted deployments customers may elect a dedicated tenancy option; for Private deployments we support air-gapped installs.

3) Logs captured (examples)
- admin.activity: { timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, target_type, target_id, request_id, ip_address, user_agent, rule_triggered }
- api.request: { timestamp, request_id, path, method, status, response_time_ms, actor_id, payload_hash }
- service.events: operational events (scales/rollouts/errors) with contextual metadata

4) Exportability & formats
- Delivery targets: S3/GCS/Azure Blob or secure FTP.
- Formats: JSONL (full fidelity), Parquet/CSV (columnar view) — we can produce a signed manifest (SHA256 checksums + timestamp) with each export.

5) Immutability & provenance
- We support export workflows designed for immutability: exports can be placed into an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled and a signed manifest to support tamper-evidence. For on-prem/private installs we can integrate with customer-provided WORM storage.
- We also provide a chain-of-custody PDF that summarizes export parameters and export timestamps for audit purposes.

6) Retention & legal hold
- Default hosted admin log retention: 24 months (configurable per-account).
- We can create export snapshots for legal hold and maintain separate archival retention policies (e.g., 1, 2, 5 years) depending on contract.

7) Sensitive fields & redaction
- Exports can be configured to exclude raw payloads or to redact specific fields. Where payloads are required, we include payload hashes and a minimal redaction plan so forensic teams have verifiable evidence without unnecessary PHI exposure.

8) Sample API (how to request an export)
- Console flow: Admin > Activity exports > New export (choose timeframe, event types, destination)
- API call: POST /v1/exports with JSON body (timeRange, events, destination.s3, objectLock:true) — returns export_id and signed manifest on completion.

9) Next steps I propose
- If you confirm: (A) desired retention window (you mentioned 24 months), (B) whether you need full payloads or hashes-only, and (C) preferred export destination (S3/GCS) — we’ll prep a demo that includes an end-to-end export (create export, verify manifest, show object lock).

References: I’ve uploaded a short technical doc and an example export to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_redwood-clearpath-audit
Also linking the HubSpot deal for tracking: https://hubspot.example/deal/CPH-2024-09

Happy to answer any questions prior to the demo.

— Marissa Cole
